summary: Changed: fees low 43 -> 41, high 43 -> 112; added 50A, 173 sites, season May 1-Oct 20, showers, laundry, dump, ResNexus url. Confirmed sewer/water, phone. Lakefront holds on the shoreline rows, with a caveat flag.
flags: GATE FACTS: posted rate 'start at $43/night' (2026, rates page read 2026-10-16); engine $41 on a two-night weeknight stay in May or September 2027, water/electric 30A. $49 for a single Friday in May. A single weeknight is $61, $20 above the two-night rate. Passes the US$50 gate on $41. Good Sam: dossier false/absent, not re-checked. Gateway: none within 40 km (Cuyahoga Valley NP 48 km). Presence: operator site + ResNexus + 330-898-8080; Google 4.0 from 329 reviews, phone (330) 898-8080. No review summary text loaded.
PRICE CAVEAT: the $41 only applies to inland W/E sites 5-16. On summer weekends even those run $74-84, which is what most stays would pay.

WATERFRONT (lakefront kept, caveat): the map's shoreline rows are 142-156 and 157-173; imagery shows rigs in an open row at the east and south shores, within roughly 10-30 m of the water. All are named '$3750/$4000 Seasonal Site'; the engine offered 138-139, 142-153 and 154-156, 171 for 5/18/2027 at $79 ($120 for 171) and fewer in August ($112; 171 at $245). 157-170, 172, 173 weren't offered on either date, so they may be contracted. The plain RV sites 1-26, 81-101 aren't on the lake. A summer booking may find no shoreline site, and I can't tell what 2027 contracts will leave open.

LONG-STAY TEST 4: passes. 31 RV + 16 tent of about 190 sites (roughly 1 in 4) are typed for nightly use, and most seasonal-named sites were also offered by the night in May. Monthly stays 'at our regular nightly rates'. Seasonal $2,500-$4,000 for 2026.

SITE WALL: gathergroundsresorts.com now shows 'Confirm you are human' to the browser and a rate-limit page to plain HTTP. I didn't click through; the operator's text above is from the price pass's 2026-10-16 read, so the amenities page and rig length weren't re-read. Pin OK at the beach/office side of the lake.
